model.name: Feature typed unit type + FeatureManager root-of-trust — product layer linking implementations to user grants
model.description: Tron model (2026-07-21, brief 0427d264f) + architect security design 83836631a (APPROVED rulings). ior:class:Feature is a first-class TYPED scenario unit = the PRODUCT layer: {name, description, icon, implementations[] (BOTH-WAY: Impl.feature back-ref, mirror-maintained), allowedUsers[] (-> profile TOKENS, BOTH-WAY with profile.features)}. Two instances: ServerManager (the R31.1-R31.4 feature) + FeatureManager (grant/revoke Features on profiles, root-of-trust). Generalizes R31.1 (profile renders granted-Feature list off m.features, server-computed) + R31.2 (access = requireFeatureAccess = isLiveSession AND user-in-Feature.allowedUsers, data-driven). SECURITY (architect-owned, finalized off 83836631a): FeatureManager grant-editing = HARDCODED owner-gate (root-of-trust, NOT data-driven = closes self-grant escalation); feature ACCESS = data-driven allowedUsers, AND-composed with isLiveSession; OWNER_TOKEN literal used ONLY for root-of-trust + bootstrap seed (==1 preserved, no literal-bypass into feature-access — owner enters via seeded membership); bootstrap idempotent-seeds OWNER_TOKEN into ServerManager+FeatureManager allowedUsers; INV-F5 empty/malformed allowedUsers FAILS CLOSED. Preserves R31.2 INV-G1/G2/G3 (grants only ADD checks). Route: req formalizes (this) -> expert implements (Feature units + Impl.feature back-refs + profile.features + requireFeatureAccess + FeatureManager grant/revoke owner-gated + bootstrap seed + m.features render) -> tester gates (both-way nav; grant/revoke flips member-200/non-member-403; profile lists granted; INV-F1..5 hold). TRON CLARIFICATION 2026-07-22 (capture-gate, architect-confirmed 83836631a, PO-approved): slice-(b+) MINT-GENERALIZATION — /session mint generalizes to 'any LIVE authenticated user mints a session carrying THEIR OWN token' (non-privileged binding); grant/revoke stays hardcoded-owner (root-of-trust); access = per-feature allowedUsers; INV-G re-verified under generalized mint (non-owner-WITH-session STILL 403 on ServerManager, gated by allowedUsers not session-absence). Without this, allowedUsers is inert (no non-owner could hold a session to be checked) — the Feature model wouldn't actually work for non-owners. +AC-mint-generalization. TRON CLARIFICATION 2026-07-22 (capture-gate, v0.7.107): FeatureManager RENDERS but does NOT OPEN on tap — the FeatureManager entry must OPEN into an admin VIEW (currently none). +AC-featuremanager-view: tap -> FeatureManager view in the DEFAULT DRAWER (consistent w/ ServerManager + R31.4 drawer DRY); lists each Feature + its allowedUsers; owner grants (by link-code/token) + revokes via the PROVEN grant/revoke API (POST /api/feature-manager, owner-gated); owner-only opens/uses (requireFeatureAccess). UC/Method for the view to be minted scenario-first from the architect's topology (design coordination requested, #126). TRON CLARIFICATION 2026-07-22 (capture-gate, IMG_4614): FeatureManager grant input = replace the raw player-token field with a USER SELECTOR + c2-style completion — type name/email/phone/uuid -> suggest matching user PROFILES (shown with identifying detail, see-the-profile) -> select -> Grant; multi-key resolve to the token via the existing phone/email alternate-UUID + profile data; owner-gated search+grant; same for revoke where useful. +AC-grant-user-selector. UC/Method (userSearch + selector) to be minted scenario-first from architect topology (design coordination requested, #126). TRON ADDENDUM 2026-07-22 (capture-gate, same AC): the matched-user DETAILED profile view REUSES the shared rb-detail-drawer (DRY, no new component) — selecting/expanding a suggestion opens the detailed profile IN the shared drawer, consistent with ServerManager/FeatureManager/trace detail-views. Folded into AC-grant-user-selector. TRON DRY REFRAME 2026-07-22 (capture-gate): the FeatureManager view = SHARED rb-trace-tree + rb-detail-drawer (like /server-manager), NOT a bespoke list. Features=items, granted-users=child-items; grant=add child-item (c2 selector), revoke=remove child-item, item-detail=shared drawer. SUPERSEDES the card-list. Folded into AC-featuremanager-view + AC-grant-user-selector. Chain reconciliation (architect R31.8c design, per-node topology on request): RETIRE/repoint mount b7d6ca6a (list superseded by tree), KEEP applyGrant ee4143df, RESHAPE listFeatures 5e338054 to itemView roots; NEW nodes = FeatureManager.searchUsers + RbFeatureManagerDetail.userComplete + RbProfileDetail.mount + a feature-detail; tagMap profile->rb-profile-detail (new) + feature->rb-feature-detail. TRON REFINEMENT 2026-07-22 (capture-gate, maximally-DRY): Features ARE typed scenario units (ior:class:Feature) — the FeatureManager tree renders them via the EXISTING scenario-unit itemView, NOT a reshaped API list. Feature unit=node, allowedUsers refs=child items; grant=add ref, revoke=remove ref, itemView re-renders from the unit. IMPLICATION for reconciliation (architect): listFeatures 5e338054 RESHAPE-to-itemView-roots may be SUPERSEDED (units render natively) rather than reshaped — flag to architect for the node-topology call. Folded into AC-featuremanager-view. SECURITY GAP 2026-07-22 (expert-discovered v0.7.112, bottom-up — not a Tron quote): the R31.8c native-render wired /api/trace/children to resolve Feature allowedUsers children (composite refs carrying the token) WITHOUT owner-gating -> member tokens leak to non-owners (violates INV-F1/masked-PII). +AC-trace-children-owner-gated: owner-gate /api/trace/children on Features + non-owner->403 + no token-bearing ref to non-owners; architect to decide the gating + whether the composite ref drops the raw token (userUuid instead). BLOCKS R31.8c functional-done until fixed+gated. TRON CAPTURE-GATE 2026-07-22: FeatureManager lists ALL enabled users (Feature.allowedUsers) as itemView CHILDREN of the feature, on load. Assessment (Rule 9): MOSTLY COVERED by AC-featuremanager-view (allowedUsers=children, complete, native itemView) + the uncapped allowedUsersChildren resolver (MEASURED: au.map over full allowedUsers, no slice/cap); SHARPENED with explicit +AC-featuremanager-lists-all-members to pin the on-load COMPLETENESS testably (N allowedUsers -> exactly N children on expand, no subset/cap) for the functional gate. Architect measurement coordinated (no cap in built impl). TRON DEVICE-FEEDBACK 2026-07-22 (capture-gate, IMG_4616 @390, R31.8c FUNCTIONAL confirmed working): "thats not bad, but it should be itemviews to the user scenario not additional uuids and in the details the users profile... the Revoke button is good - do the actions directly under the drawerbar and all further content below." 3 refinements captured: +AC-children-itemview-user-scenario (children = itemviews bound to user scenario, ref stays opaque per FIX-2, resolve server-side) + AC-detail-full-profile (drawer detail = full RbProfileDetail profile, not name+id+button) + AC-drawer-actions-layout (grab-bar->actions->content). Architect coordinates design/topology (itemview-bound resolution + RbProfileDetail full-render + actions-under-bar layout on shared rb-detail-drawer) before finalize. TRON/ARCHITECT 2026-07-22 (capture-gate): +AC-inv-f7-server-side-resolve — INV-F7: allowedUsersChildren + grantedUserProfile resolve userId->token->profile SERVER-SIDE; response carries ONLY masked display (name/avatar/masked-ids), NEVER raw token or secretCode; opaque FIX-2 ref preserved; GET /api/feature-manager/granted-user owner-gated (requireFeatureAccess Feature Manager); Revoke stays hardcoded-owner (INV-F4). + minted grantedUserProfile chain (UC featureManager.viewGrantedUser -> Method grantedUserProfile on FeatureManager 9f7f345a). TRON DEVICE-FEEDBACK ROUND 2 2026-07-23 (capture-gate): 'the real profile. good. ... full uuid not a truncated phone ... tree must update automatically ... latest on Refresh ... eager lazy ... collapsed still show correct children not 0 ... revoke directly under the drawer bar and then the full existing profileviewer ... reread the requirements i said. they included it already the first time.' HONEST GATE-GAP: round-1 AC-detail-full-profile + AC-drawer-actions-layout were captured but shipped as a name+truncated-phone STUB and the gate passed the WRONG surface (flow, not rendered @390) -> BOTH RE-OPENED status=reopened-unmet, do NOT re-close until built AND rendered-gated @390. +3 NEW ACs each pinned to a RENDERED @390 assertion: AC-item-description-full-uuid, AC-tree-auto-update-on-action, AC-collapsed-child-count-eager. Architect coordinates DRY reuse of the existing profile-viewer + the SHARED eager/lazy tree child-count mechanic (no fork). [[gate-the-ac-surface]] [[generic-behavior-in-the-shared-component]] PO ADD 2026-07-23: capture the impl approach on AC-detail-full-profile (delivered by EXTRACTING new shared RbProfileView — no reusable client viewer existed, hence round-1 stub; shared/masking-aware/INV-F7-by-construction) + new SCOPED FAST-FOLLOW AC-profile-single-viewer-fastfollow (migrate /profile to <rb-profile-view> = ONE viewer, not round-2-blocking but owned). TRON RULING 2026-07-23 (capture-gate, 10cf5cd3d) — AC-item-description-full-uuid RESOLVED: the granted-user item description = the OPAQUE userId (FIX-2 sha256(token)[:16]), NOT the raw token, NOT a separate profile-scenario uuid (Tron: it's the stable, non-sensitive, already-URL-addressable id; preserves INV-F7 by construction; safe under future non-owner delegation; display '<name> / <opaque-userId>'). This LIFTS the earlier HOLD on impl-edit (a) allowedUsersChildren desc=full-uuid (ad622052) — the form is now opaque userId sha256[:16]. ROUND-3 (architect design 0cd05131a, DELIVER LITERALLY) — Tron device-REJECTED round-2's masked/opaque surface (the scope-creep WE injected: sha256 uuid, masked mini-card, INV-F7-owner-masking, deferred /profile migration = the stub). Round-3 refines the ACs: subtitle = REAL profile/User-unit uuid (supersedes opaque sha256); drawer = REAL FULL data no-mask (supersedes masked subset); INV-F7 owner-masking WITHDRAWN (keep non-owner→403, the real P0); /profile MIGRATES NOW to <rb-profile-view> (drawer == /profile viewer = proof, ACTIVATES the ex-fast-follow); +AC-token-profileuuid-resolver (retires userIdOf-sha256/resolveGrantedToken/grantedAvatarUrl-opaque). The round-2 opaque + masked ACs are superseded IN PLACE with provenance (no silent overwrite). Tester gates @390 vs the /profile REFERENCE. RESOLVER PINNED AUTHORITATIVE (architect 3fedd1337): profileUuidOf = follow consolidation (redirectTo→primary) → primary Profile-unit's own uuid; tokenOfProfileUuid = uuid-is-a-token (Profile units token-keyed). HARD RULE: no hash, no hardcoded 37fcb752, no invented field — ONLY existing consolidation. The rich distinct uuid appears IFF consolidated; absent consolidation the resolver honestly returns the token-keyed uuid (owner 41ad88c4 today). Showing the owner his rich 37fcb752 = a SEPARATE Tron/PO consolidation data-decision (option B), NOT the resolver — architect flagged it to PO. My earlier 'Marcel=37fcb752' example was over-specific; corrected: the subtitle == profileUuidOf(token) output, asserted @390 against the resolver result (not a hardcoded value). CONSOLIDATION RESOLVED (Tron ruling 448f6837f, capture-gate): Tron authorized the one-time link 41ad88c4 → 37fcb752 via the existing redirectTo/consolidation mechanism (option B, architect-recommended; NOT option-A re-key). So the resolver ships as pinned (2b4d7151b) and, once the architect-specified consolidation action is executed by the expert on Tron's profiles, profileUuidOf(41ad88c4) follows redirectTo → 37fcb752 correct-by-construction. Recorded on AC-item-description-full-uuid as the resolution: the fix is a DATA consolidation, not a display change; @390 asserts subtitle == profileUuidOf output (37fcb752 AFTER consolidation), never a hardcoded value. ⚠ CONSOLIDATE RECORD HELD — PREMISE INVERTED (architect measurement c99c49598, PO 2026-07-23): the prior Tron consolidate ruling (448f6837f, recorded 6cb29ede3) was on a BACKWARDS premise. 41ad88c4 is ALREADY Tron's PRIMARY consolidated identity (chain 37fcb752 → 8f74dfba → 41ad88c4); forcing 41ad88c4 → 37fcb752 would redirect the primary to a tombstone and FAIL assertOwner = lock Tron out. So: NO consolidation is executed; the resolver already returns 41ad88c4 CORRECTLY (no mutation). AC-item-description-full-uuid resolution = PENDING-TRON-RE-DECISION (PO taking the corrected picture to Tron). The 448f6837f ruling is kept in history (Rule 11) but is SUPERSEDED/HELD by the inverted-premise finding — do NOT lock in the consolidate record. The resolver + all other round-3 ACs are unaffected; only the owner's target-uuid display awaits Tron's re-decision. ROUND-4 (Tron device walk-through 2026-07-23, R31.8c-round4-feedback.md, capture-gate) — the gate-gap struck again: round-3 gated GREEN @390 on /profile-render + a SEEDED/STRUCTURAL view, NOT Tron's REAL interactive owner session, so it missed: the drawer is a FORK (≠ /profile, NO Devices list), Revoke doesn't live-update the tree, Refresh is a no-op, a stray 'no graph' label. RE-OPENED AC-detail-full-profile as UNMET (drawer must === /profile incl Devices(N)). +4 ACs each pinned to a REAL INTERACTIVE @390 assertion (not flow/structural): AC-revoke-live-tree-update, AC-reactive-always-no-refresh (★ Tron standing principle: NEVER need Refresh; reactive-always, Refresh=last-resort), AC-refresh-fallback-works, AC-no-stray-graph-label. LIKELY ONE ROOT (architect to confirm): the FM tree is not backed by a reactive/live data source → fix once (reactive data source + drawer shares BOTH view AND data feed with /profile), reuse the SHARED itemView/tree mechanics, NO per-symptom fork. Re-gate MUST drive the REAL owner-interactive flow (seed owner session, actually click Revoke, observe live tree change, side-by-side drawer-vs-/profile screenshots) — not seeded-structural. ROOTS CONFIRMED (architect f94875f6e + PO refine): ROOT A = ONE root for issues 2/3/4/5 (reactive tree): A1 /api/feature-manager returns allowedUsers INLINE (like /server-manager) → shared renderItems reconciles grant/revoke LIVE (reactive; refresh=last-resort honored); A2 items-tree skips the graph ViewBus sub + clears the stale 'no graph' placeholder (SHARED rb-trace-tree fix). ROOT B = issue 1 is NOT a component fork — the FEED differs (grantedUserProfile summary/no-devices vs /profile full/devices); FIX = extract ONE shared profileViewData(full incl devices) builder used by BOTH → drawer===/profile by construction, INV-F7 kept. Node topology (architect, #126): FIX-A1 impl-edit featureRoots (inline allowedUsers, reuse allowedUsersChildren, NO new node); FIX-A2 impl-edit SHARED rb-trace-tree (existing render/renderItems/connectedCallback Impls, NO new node); FIX-B NEW shared Method profileViewData + impl-edits grantedUserProfile + /profile. req mints FIX-B scenario-first (topology requested from architect), reconciles the A1/A2 impl-edits. ROUND-4 CLOSED (PO 2026-07-23): all 6 device-QA ACs FLIPPED to MET, honestly — GREEN DET-3x @390 REAL owner-interactive + screenshot-verified (a2be85f4e v0.7.127), not structural. 2 round-4 Tests minted (c471d275→c3e6a2b4 devices-parity/drawer===profile; 147da46d→c5b331a7 reactive revoke-live+badge). 0 rejected-surface Tests. The feed-not-fork root (shared ProfileView.profileViewData) + reactive setItems (skip graph-sub) fixed the drawer-fork + revoke-no-live-update + stray-no-graph at once. Only Tron device re-verify remains to close R31.8c.
model.tronQuote: > TRON (2026-07-21): "model a scenario-first unit type Feature. it is referenced by all implementations. so ServerManager is a feature and itself references all implementations belonging to it… so both-way consistent navigation. additionally it references the user's scenarios that are allowed to use it from the user profile. a second feature on the same rights as the server manager is the FeatureManager, that allows to enable and disable features on user profiles. add a list of features to my profile this way where the server manager is currently."

discoverySource.flaggedBy: Tron (2026-07-21) via robbin-po (brief 0427d264f); security by robbin-architect (83836631a)
discoverySource.note: Feature typed unit + FeatureManager root-of-trust; security/bootstrap coordinated with architect per PO before finalizing ACs.

acceptanceCriteria.text: ior:class:Feature is a first-class TYPED scenario unit (FeatureModel schema): name, description, icon, implementations[] (refs to Impl units), allowedUsers[] (refs to user profile TOKENS — profiles are Map+JSON today, server.ts:166; token is the stable identity; full profile-as-unit = later migration). The PRODUCT layer linking code to user grants.

INV-F-MIRROR: Feature.implementations[] <-> Impl.feature both-way — for every f in Feature.implementations, Impl(f).feature==Feature; Feature->its impls AND impl->its Feature both resolve. Mirror-maintained like Class.methods[]/Method.ownerIor; a drift-check fails loud.

Feature.allowedUsers[] <-> profile.features[] (new UserProfile field, Feature-uuid refs) both-way — a grant writes BOTH sides atomically, a revoke removes from BOTH. Feature->its users AND user->their features both resolve.

Two S31 Feature instances: ServerManager (implementations=[assertOwner impl 335dbf3d, attachPane 394eac63, readSessionTree 5c1701bc, renderFeatureGrants f345b8ed, buildSeedNode 5b3d9f1a, reapOrphans 5d313828 — representative, architect-refined]; allowedUsers=[Tron 41ad88c4]) + FeatureManager (function: enable/disable Features on profiles = grant/revoke; implementations to-be-built; allowedUsers=[Tron]).

REFRAMES R31.1: replace the single serverManager flag (server.ts:2625) with features:<Feature[] where token in allowedUsers> on the PROFILE ws msg (server-computed, same trust path, client can't self-grant). renderFeatureGrants iterates m.features -> one entry per granted Feature (name/icon/link) at #feature-grants. Tron -> [ServerManager, FeatureManager]; non-granted -> empty -> section ABSENT by construction (not UI-hidden).

REFRAMES R31.2 (architect design 83836631a): feature ACCESS = requireFeatureAccess(req, featureName) = isLiveSession(token) AND token in Feature.allowedUsers — data-driven membership, AND-composed (both fail-closed), replacing the hardcoded per-feature owner-gate. Added at the SAME server-side choke (server.ts:891 pattern), never bypassed; UI-hiding is NOT the gate. INV-F1: every feature's routes+ws -> 403 for non-members.

INV-F4 (root-of-trust): FeatureManager grant/revoke — ANY write to allowedUsers/profile.features — is gated by the HARDCODED owner-gate (ServerManagerGuard.assertOwner / the R31.2 OWNER_TOKEN literal), NOT data-driven. A data-driven-only path to grant-editing is the escalation HOLE (anyone reaching FeatureManager could self-add to any feature) and is REJECTED. Only the hardcoded owner mutates grants; a non-owner grant attempt -> 403, never mutates.

BOOTSTRAP + INV-F5: at first run an idempotent seed writes OWNER_TOKEN into ServerManager.allowedUsers AND FeatureManager.allowedUsers from the hardcoded literal (a generated seed step, R31.7-aligned) — the hardcoded owner is the bootstrap root, from there Tron grants others via FeatureManager; NO grant path exists that doesn't originate at the hardcoded owner. INV-F5: a feature with EMPTY/MALFORMED allowedUsers FAILS CLOSED (403 for all, incl owner-unless-seeded), NEVER fails-open.

R31.2 INV-G preserved, NOT weakened: INV-G1 stays ONE server-side choke (now calls requireFeatureAccess(feature), not requireOwnerHttp); INV-G2 the OWNER_TOKEN literal stays ==1 (used ONLY for the FeatureManager root-of-trust + bootstrap seed; feature access adds NO new literals, uses allowedUsers data; grep-guard still ==1); INV-F3 (=INV-G3) a feature ws upgrade checks requireFeatureAccess BEFORE handleUpgrade, non-member -> socket.destroy before open. The OWNER reaches ServerManager via seeded allowedUsers MEMBERSHIP (same data path as any grantee) — NO literal-bypass OR into feature-access.

The /session mint GENERALIZES: any LIVE authenticated user mints a session carrying THEIR OWN token (non-privileged binding — the session binds the caller's own identity, NOT an owner privilege). Grant/revoke stays HARDCODED-owner (root-of-trust, INV-F4); feature ACCESS = per-feature allowedUsers (requireFeatureAccess). INV-G RE-VERIFIED under the generalized mint: a non-owner WITH a live session is STILL 403 on ServerManager — gated by allowedUsers MEMBERSHIP, NOT by session-absence (the session existing does not grant access; allowedUsers does). This makes the Feature model actually WORK for non-owners (else allowedUsers is inert — no non-owner could ever hold a session to be membership-checked).

Tapping the FeatureManager entry in the profile Feature-access list OPENS the FeatureManager VIEW (v0.7.107 BUG: FeatureManager RENDERS in the list but does NOT open on tap — no view exists). The view MOUNTS in the DEFAULT DRAWER (consistent with ServerManager + the R31.4 drawer direction / the DRY shared detail-flow, NOT a bespoke overlay). The view LISTS each Feature + its granted users (allowedUsers). The OWNER grants a feature to a user (by link-code / token) AND revokes — backed by the PROVEN grant/revoke API (POST /api/feature-manager, owner-gated; the slice-(b) grantFeature/revokeFeature 5e2f6781/987a31a9). OWNER-ONLY opens/uses it (owner in FeatureManager.allowedUsers, enforced by requireFeatureAccess — NOT UI-hiding). ★ DRY TREE-VIEW REFRAME (Tron, supersedes the card-list): the FeatureManager view IS a TREE on the SHARED rb-trace-tree (like ServerManager otmux tree) — Features = ITEMS (root nodes), granted-users (allowedUsers) = CHILD ITEMS under each Feature node. Item-detail (feature node / user node) opens in the shared rb-detail-drawer. NO bespoke list/cards. The card-list framing above is SUPERSEDED. ★★ MAXIMALLY-DRY (Tron): the tree renders the Feature SCENARIO UNITS (ior:class:Feature) via the EXISTING scenario-unit itemView (NOT a reshaped API list) — the Feature UNIT is the node, its allowedUsers refs are the CHILD ITEMS; GRANT = ADD an allowedUsers ref to the unit, REVOKE = REMOVE the ref, and the itemView RE-RENDERS natively from the unit. Scenario units render themselves (same mechanism /trace uses) — no bespoke render, no API-list reshape.

The FeatureManager grant input is a USER SELECTOR with c2-style COMPLETION, replacing the raw 'player token to grant' field. Typing a name / email / phone / UUID completes/suggests matching USER PROFILES, each shown with identifying detail (SEE the profile, like c2 Tab-completion); selecting one -> Grant. MULTI-KEY resolve: name / email / phone / uuid -> the user token (leveraging the existing phone/email alternate-UUID + profile data). OWNER-GATED for BOTH search and grant (requireFeatureAccess / owner-gate; the search endpoint is owner-only, never leaks profiles to non-owners). Applies to the revoke side too where useful. PROFILE DETAIL REUSES THE SHARED DRAWER (DRY, no new component): selecting/expanding a matched user in the selector opens their DETAILED PROFILE in the shared rb-detail-drawer — consistent with the ServerManager / FeatureManager / trace detail-views (same shared detail-flow, not a bespoke popup). ★ TREE FRAMING (Tron): GRANT = ADD a user CHILD-ITEM under the Feature node (via the c2-completion user selector); REVOKE = REMOVE the child-item. The matched-user detailed profile opens in the shared rb-detail-drawer (tagMap profile->rb-profile-detail). Consistent with the shared item/itemView tree, no bespoke cards.

/api/trace/children on a Feature unit (it resolves allowedUsers via allowedUsersChildren, emitting COMPOSITE member refs that carry the user TOKEN) MUST be OWNER-GATED (INV-F): a non-owner GET -> 403, and token-bearing composite member refs are NEVER emitted to non-owners. ALSO evaluate whether the composite ref should carry the RAW TOKEN at all (token in a URL-addressable ref leaks via logs/history) — prefer a non-token composite (e.g. profile:<featureUuid>:<userUuid>) resolved server-side, per architect security design. Expert-discovered gap (v0.7.112): the native-render wired /api/trace/children to resolve Feature children WITHOUT owner-gating, leaking member tokens to non-owners — violates INV-F1 (owner-only) + masked-PII. The FUNCTIONAL tester gate MUST include this: non-owner /api/trace/children on a Feature -> 403, no token leak. ★ RESOLVED (architect 2919770c3, BOTH THIN no-new-node): (1) OWNER-GATE = thin wire of the EXISTING requireFeatureAccess (35e91ba7) into the /api/trace/children type===Feature branch (server.ts:1499) BEFORE returning children -> non-member/non-owner 403 (membership-gated Feature Manager, consistent w/ the view+GET; non-Feature units stay public). RELEASE-BLOCKER, gate FIRST. (2) DROP-RAW-TOKEN = impl-edit on allowedUsersChildren 72c660f9: composite ref = profile:<featureUuid>:<userId> (STABLE NON-TOKEN id), server resolves userId->token for display+revoke; the raw AUTH TOKEN NEVER rides a URL-addressable ref (defense-in-depth). Both impl-edits, expert wires. Functional gate asserts: non-owner /api/trace/children on a Feature -> 403 + no token in any emitted ref.

On expand/load of a Feature node in the FeatureManager tree, ALL of that Feature enabled users render as itemView CHILD nodes — a Feature with N allowedUsers shows EXACTLY N child user-nodes (COMPLETENESS: no subset, no cap/pagination-drop, no manual-refresh required). Resolved by allowedUsersChildren (72c660f9/Impl ad622052) which maps over the FULL Feature.allowedUsers (measured: no slice/cap in the built impl — unlike searchUsers which is capped-10, because MEMBERS are the authoritative set and must be complete), rendered NATIVELY via the existing itemView (CHAIN_TYPE_CONFIG Feature.scenarioFwd:[allowedUsers]). Owner-gated (AC-trace-children-owner-gated). Tester functional gate asserts N-in -> N-children on load at Tron viewport.

The granted-user CHILD nodes under a Feature are itemviews BOUND TO the user SCENARIO unit (the person profile), NOT standalone opaque-uuid rows (device IMG_4616: children were generic uuid rows, subtitle just repeated the name). The itemview resolves + navigates to the REAL user. ★ SECURITY (architect-owned, preserves FIX-2): the URL-addressable ref STAYS OPAQUE (<featureUuid>:<sha256(token)[:16]>, no raw token) — the itemview resolves the user SERVER-SIDE (owner-gated) for display/nav; do NOT re-expose the token to satisfy itemview-to-user-scenario. Display resolves the user; the ref stays hashed.

⚠ RE-OPENED UNMET (round-4 device-QA, Tron 2026-07-23): round-3 shipped a FORK, not the identical /profile viewer. The FM drawer render MUST === the /profile render — SAME sections INCLUDING the Devices(N) list with FULL details (Mac/deviceId, IP, resolution, Nx-connected, Last-timestamp), same fields (avatar / name / Token / Secret Code / Devices(N) / Feature-access), same layout. The round-3 drawer showed 'Profile UUID / Token / Identifiers / Secret Code / Feature grants' + NO Devices list = a DIFFERENT layout/fields (different component OR data-shape OR conditional render) — the 'same rb-profile-view' claim was FALSE at the render surface. @390 GATE (REAL owner-interactive, NOT seeded-structural): side-by-side SCREENSHOT match drawer-vs-/profile — same sections incl the Devices(N) list — not merely 'a component named rb-profile-view mounted'. Ref: R31.8c-round4-drawer-fork vs R31.8c-round4-profile-reference. ★ ROOT (confirmed, architect f94875f6e + PO): this is NOT a component fork — the COMPONENT is shared; the DATA FEED differs (grantedUserProfile returns a SUMMARY / no-devices shape vs /profile's FULL / devices shape). FIX = extract ONE shared profileViewData(full, incl a devices builder) used by BOTH grantedUserProfile AND /profile → drawer === /profile BY CONSTRUCTION (same component + same data shape).
